correctness.rationale: Every initial-color cohort in one shore remains homogeneous. Replacing its population m by min(2,m) preserves the threshold-two predicate and the list of occupied cohorts, hence both exact first-entry and primitive period. This yields 26^3=17,576 exhaustive tagged signatures. The standalone program independently reconstructs their minimal labelled graphs and verifies matching exact stopping times for all signatures. Exact checks confirm periods {1,3,4,12}, maximum transient 11, sharp existence predicates on every sorted triple of sizes 1..7, and the feasibility lemma that each shore size >=7 permits precisely capped triples containing a 2. Four extra exhaustive labelled censuses cross-check the coefficient formula. The finite test is exhaustive because the reduction and cutoff are proved.

value.rationale: Exact first-entry distributions and sharp onsets/disappearance of primitive three-, four-, and twelve-cycles are natural structural dynamical invariants. The nonmonotone period-twelve window persists with arbitrarily large two shores but disappears completely once the smallest shore reaches four; this is not routine from prior two-shore spectra. The global eleven-step bound is sharp and the coefficient formula gives all labelled populations on the infinite graph family.
